Audio Transfer

Move a small file from one browser’s speaker through the air to another browser’s microphone. Filename, size, session identity, CRC32C-protected chunks, and SHA-256 all travel acoustically—there is no payload upload, relay, pairing server, account, or network data path.

Audible transmission: this tool intentionally plays a modem-like 1.5–5.5 kHz signal. Start at a comfortable device volume, keep speakers away from ears, and stop if the sound is uncomfortable. The waveform targets conservative 0.08 RMS / 0.50 peak before the page’s output gain. Acoustic v1 is plaintext: anyone in earshot with a compatible receiver may recover the file.

Send through the speaker

Files may contain any binary bytes and are limited to 64 KB. The sender emits the manifest five times, every 256-byte data chunk twice in opposite orders, and the final identity three times so isolated packet loss does not require a return channel.

What the speaker sends

Audible C0 OFDM uses a deterministic preamble, BPSK carriers, pilots, a K=7 rate-1/2 convolutional code, interleaving, duplicated protected headers, and CRC32C. Each physical packet is bounded to four seconds. Output and capture run in an AudioWorklet at the observed 44.1 or 48 kHz context rate.

Receive from the microphone

Receive asks only for microphone permission. Hosted HTTPS is the reliable mobile path; installing or revisiting the Local Suite PWA once keeps this page available offline on that secure origin.

Integrity and privacy boundary

A receiver locks to one nonzero 128-bit session and one SHA-256 manifest identity. CRC32C-invalid packets never enter reconstruction; conflicting duplicates fail the transfer. Progress reaches 100% and the download link appears only after every declared byte is present, the repeated final identity agrees, and Web Crypto reproduces the acoustically declared SHA-256.

Local processing only. No payload, metadata, microphone sample, or transfer progress is sent to a server or stored persistently. AudioWorklet, modem Worker, microphone tracks, AudioContext, queues, temporary URLs, and stale callbacks are stopped or revoked on Stop, Reset, tab changes, completion, and page exit.
